extracted.intended_audience: general readers and media professionals interested in television news formats / local broadcast news
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and descriptive criteria for producing or judging an 'anchor-less' local television newscast in the NewsFix / newsreel style (format, production, content, audience, and success metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchor-less narration-based presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: De-emphasizes the use of news anchors to present the stories featured during the broadcast, opting to instead use footage involving the story with illustration on the story being reported through narration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an off-camera narrator for continuity rather than on-air anchors or reporters; eliminates traditional anchor presentation and on-air reporter appearances. Example: continuity narrator (Greg Onofrio) plus narration for story packages. Anti-pattern: relying on anchors and 'happy talk' between blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsreel / long-form format
rubrics_metrics.description: Used a long-form format similar to a newsreel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure stories as packaged visual segments in a newsreel style rather than live-anchor-driven pieces. Emphasize visual storytelling and packaged reports over live desk segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primarily video-footage-led stories filmed by photojournalists
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories presented primarily through video footage filmed by photojournalists employed by both stations and filed from affiliate news video services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on photojournalists to shoot, write and edit packaged stories. Avoid anchor-live reads; prioritize engaging visuals shot on scene. Production implication: requires photojournalist workflow rather than traditional reporter/anchor roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted younger demographic (ages 12–34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted at a younger demographic (specifically those aged 12 to 34) that may receive news through online and other digital services rather than through television.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design pacing, content choices, visuals, and music to appeal to younger viewers who consume news digitally. Measure success against attraction/retention in that demographic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faster-paced format and high segment density
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintains a faster-paced format than conventional television newscasts, incorporating an average of 33 segments per broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for short, rapid segments with quick transitions; high segment count favors breadth and tempo over deep, long-form single stories. Scoring consideration: tempo and ability to convey information quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal 'happy talk' and increased story time
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to eliminate the 'happy talk' segments between news blocks to devote more time to stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conversational interstitials among on-air talent; maximize time spent on packaged story content. Anti-pattern: excessive banter or filler that reduces story time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual tagging and map/icon-based tosses
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses a world map augmented with markers resembling mobile app icons to identify the location and to serve as a toss to each story segment (referenced with a brief headline-style description under the icon marker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement distinctive on-screen location markers and brief headline text in place of verbal teases; use consistent visual tags to introduce segments. This supports the 'web-like' experience the format seeks to emulate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute teases with visual tags (no traditional teases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitution of teases before breaks in favor of the aforementioned visual tags to indicate segments and stories set to air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use traditional spoken teases before commercial breaks; instead rely on on-screen visual cues and headlines to indicate upcoming segments. Anti-pattern: traditional tease structure that slows pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contemporary music instead of traditional theme music
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of contemporary music (instead of custom or pre-packaged theme music) for the program's theme music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose contemporary tracks that resonate with the target younger audience rather than classic news theme packages. Consider licensing, tone, and how music supports pacing and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited weather segment
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporates a short weather segment (limited to current weather observations and a five-day forecast).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep weather concise and functional—current conditions plus a brief five-day forecast—avoiding extended meteorological analysis or long-form weather features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited sports coverage (scores-only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sports segment consisting mainly of scores, omitting highlights or game commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quick scoreboard-style sports updates without extended game highlights or analysis to maintain pace and fit the segment-density model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring feature segments (Crime Bureau, Day in Pictures, Day in Music)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporates features such as 'Crime Bureau' (formatted similarly to a police blotter with photos of criminals on the run), 'Day in Pictures' (featuring photographs of news stories and happenings in each city) and a historical music segment, 'Day in Music'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design recurring branded features that fit short-segment format: visual crime briefs, photo montages, and themed music history bits. Use these to provide variety and predictable hooks for viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrator commentary segment at broadcast end
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrators ... also deliver a commentary segment at the end of each broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a short closing commentary by the narrator to provide perspective or a signature sign-off. Scoring: effectiveness and tone of commentary relative to overall program voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller/staff-efficient production model
rubrics_metrics.description: By not using on-air anchors and reporters, it was designed to eliminate the 'happy talk' segments ... while emphasizing the use of photojournalists that write and edit each story. The format ... requiring a far smaller staff to produce the broadcasts compared to traditional local news programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt staffing that reduces on-air talent and increases production and photojournalist responsibilities; measure cost-savings and operational feasibility. Production trade-offs: reduced staff may impact live reporting and community presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia-journalist workflow option
rubrics_metrics.description: Nightcap incorporated multimedia journalists (which require a single person to film, edit and report news stories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multimedia journalists for end-to-end story production in small-staff environments. Consider training, equipment, and quality-control processes required to maintain standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production readiness and logistical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to logistical issues that needed to be assessed (including workflow reconfiguration, staff training and production upgrades), the format launch was delayed three times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for necessary workflow reconfiguration, staff training, and production upgrades when implementing the format. Plan rollout with adequate training and technical upgrades to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of stale or light/offbeat-only content (criticism/anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program was criticized for featuring stories often less current in nature, occurring the previous day and those that were light or offbeat in quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to keep stories timely and substantively newsworthy rather than predominantly light/dated items; audience retention may suffer if content appears stale or trivial. Use editorial standards to balance depth and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success measured by ratings and viewership
rubrics_metrics.description: In its first two weeks, ratings for NewsFix were lower than under KIAH's previous traditional format ... Monthly ratings for the late evening broadcast dropped from a 1.0 in April to 0.9 in the May sweeps period ... before increasing to a 1.2 in August.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the format's success with traditional broadcast metrics (Nielsen ratings, demographic ratings, sweeps comparisons) and changes in viewership over time; pay attention to target-demographic performance (e.g., 12–34).
